A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CVS research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional Appendices C and D in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes/AID4AD mapping experiments, normalization and adapter ablations, teacher comparisons, feature analyses and loss-weight sensitivity results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds an auxiliary-loss comparator, further teacher and student-capacity experiments, and weather-stratified results.

M1.justification: The proposed CVS procedure retains the frozen aerial teacher, camera student, normalization, affine adapter and MSE alignment objective. Additional teacher and student configurations are experimental variants; the default method and camera-only inference remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use nuScenes/AID4AD for the same mapping classes and 60×30 m and 100×50 m regions. Appendix D partitions the existing validation data by weather without introducing new data, tasks or input conditions.

E2.justification: Section 4.1 adds an evaluated StreamMapNet comparator using a MapTRv2-style auxiliary segmentation loss. This is an auxiliary-loss adaptation, not an evaluation of the complete MapTRv2 model. StreamMapNet remains the main baseline.

E3.justification: New experiments vary auxiliary-loss weights, add an aerial-only UNet++ teacher and compare one versus two student encoder layers. Appendix D evaluates 4,763 non-rainy and 1,218 rainy samples without retraining. Existing geographic splits, AP thresholds, regions and main training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 substantially broadens analysis of why CVS works and when its gains persist: it tests ordinary auxiliary supervision, extends teacher comparisons, checks student capacity, visualizes teacher transferability in Appendix C and evaluates weather robustness in Appendix D. The earlier normalization, feature-similarity and loss-weight analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 3 retains the same feature-distribution boxplots. Appendix D's sample counts describe validation subsets, not repeated runs.

E6.justification: Headline results and Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. Added results include auxiliary-loss mAP of 23.3, 22.4 and 22.8; UNet++ teacher/student mAP of 55.0/32.2; and no material benefit from increased student depth. Table 3 adds non-rainy StreamMapNet/CVS scores of 23.6/33.0 and rainy scores of 18.6/29.7. These extend supporting findings without revising the principal results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(6), including the adapter, alignment loss, training objective and CKA definition, are unchanged. Neither version provides additional formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about training-only aerial feature supervision, unchanged camera-only inference and stronger long-range mapping. The reported headline gains remain +3.9 and +9.9 mAP.

C2.justification: v2 refines the teacher analysis toward representation transferability and uses the depth check to argue that student capacity alone is not limiting. It adds an interpretation of weather robustness and shifts the practical limitation from imagery availability toward precise metric alignment. The single-benchmark limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents the new comparator's segmentation head, ground-truth-derived targets and tested larger loss weights, plus the student-depth comparison and UNet++ training setup. The main optimizer, learning rate, batch size, hardware and repository disclosure are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds RoadTracer, Sat2Graph and CVM-Net, distinguishing CVS from aerial map extraction and cross-view localization. The ResUNet++ reference by Jha et al. present in v1 is removed. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 condenses several introduction paragraphs, rewrites feature and teacher interpretations, revises limitations and adds two appendix subsections. The main section sequence and most methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the teacher-feature comparison in Figure 9 and weather results in Table 3. Table 2 moves from page 10 to page 11, some appendix panels are resized, and references gain colored links and page back-references. Existing result plots and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The auxiliary-loss comparison addresses an alternative explanation for CVS gains, while the additional teacher, capacity and weather analyses strengthen supporting evidence. The revised alignment limitation also makes applicability clearer. These are useful, bounded improvements: the principal findings remain unchanged, evaluation still uses one benchmark, and the new capacity result lacks numerical detail or repeated-run uncertainty.
